The core difference between agile and traditional project management lies in their approach to change and planning. Traditional methods, like Waterfall, rely on rigid, upfront planning and sequential phases, making them less adaptable to change once a project begins. In contrast, agile methodologies embrace iterative development, continuous feedback, and flexible planning, allowing teams to respond quickly to shifting requirements and uncertainties. This makes agile particularly effective in dynamic environments where adaptability and responsiveness are critical.
